Plugin Reference > http-client — HTTP Client

http-client — HTTP Client

Status (2026-10-24)The HTTP client kernel is now built into sa_std: the implementation lives in sci src/runtime/sa_http_client.zig (shipped with libsa_std.a), the declarations live in sa_std/http_client.sai, and the symbols are exactly the ABI described on this page. You do not need to install this plugin to use the full client capability (synchronous/asynchronous v2/WebSocket client/SSE); the sa_plugin_http_client project now keeps only a framework-layer wrapper. A plugin is only a wrapper for interface usage habits, and does not mean the substance should be pushed down into a plugin (see the architecture principles in the Plugin Reference Overview).
Zig 0.17This plugin is built with Zig 0.17: the 0.17 branch builds successfully with Zig 0.17 and passes the Zig unit tests; the old 0.14.1 branch is left untouched.

This page gives the complete reference for sa_plugin_http_client: its place in the plugin family and its dependency relationships, install verification commands, the sap.json capability sections and permission allowlists, the full function signatures of the v1 and v2 ABIs, and copy-ready end-to-end examples. After reading this page you can judge which function set an outbound request should use, who releases which handle, and which capabilities are explicitly declared “out of scope”.

http-client provides native HTTP/1.1, HTTPS (TLS), streaming responses, and WebSocket transport for SA programs. The v1 ABI remains usable with unchanged return values; the v2 ABI adds stable network status codes, request deadlines and response-body limits, asynchronous cancellation, and WebSocket over TCP / TLS / Unix-domain sockets.

Division of Labor with Other Plugins

  • http-server — Embedded HTTP Server: the other half, in the opposite direction. The server is responsible for inbound listening on localhost; the client only makes outbound requests. The two do not depend on each other, can be used alone, and are often paired for loopback self-testing (see the example below: the client hits a local service on 127.0.0.1).
  • vite: the dev server orchestration plugin; it depends on http-server, not http-client; static serving and SSE reuse the sa_http_server_* core API.
  • deno — Deno-Compatible API Plugin and node — Node.js Compatibility Facade: JS-ecosystem compatibility facades, at the application layer, which per their sap.json declarations reuse a small number of http-client symbols (deno declares use of sa_http_client_new / sa_http_client_req_send / sa_http_client_resp_body_slice). That is: the facades are on top, the general network capability is below.
  • sax: the UI dialect plugin, with no direct relationship to this plugin; hot reload of SAX pages is done by vite with the help of http-server.
NoteThe caliber for dependency relationships changes over time: the four-plugin joint evaluation document (docs/plugin_evaluation_cn.md, evaluation date 2026-06-15) once recorded http-client reverse-depending on node and listed it as a risk; Step 1 of docs/dependency_refactor_plan_cn.md then deleted that declaration. In the current repository, dependencies in sap.json is an empty object, and http-client is a zero-dependency leaf capability layer.

Installation and Verification

The following commands come from the Development section of the repository README.md, executed inside the plugin source directory (this plugin is designed to be used from a local development checkout):

# 在 D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_http_client 目录内
timeout 300s env SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 zig build test     # 跑 tests/plugin_test.zig 全部测试
timeout 300s env SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 zig build          # 构建共享库产物
timeout 120s env SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa plugin install --dev .
timeout 30s  env SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa plugin list     # 验证已注册
  • The Zig build uses the sibling SCI checkout (../../sci) by default; override with -Dsci-root=/absolute/path/to/sci when needed; SCI provides src/runtime/sa_net_primitives.zig.
  • After a successful build, the artifact is at zig-out/lib/libhttp-client.so (Linux x86_64) or zig-out/bin/http-client.dll (Windows x86_64), matching the artifacts field of sap.json.

sap.json Capability Sections and Permissions

Permissions are declared on a “just enough” basis; every field is listed one by one below.

Filesystem (fs)

oppathPurpose
read + metadata$PROJECT/**Reading in-project resources (e.g. a CA bundle file)
read + metadata/etc/**The system certificate directory (the evaluation document states explicitly that the purpose is certificate paths)
read + metadata$HOME/.codex-max/**The user-level configuration/credential directory
metadata$SA_PLUGINS_HOME/**Discovering its own shared resources (metadata only, reading content is not allowed)

Network (net)

urlmethods
https://*GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS (seven in total)
http://localhost
http://127.0.0.1

Note that plaintext HTTP is allowed only for the two local addresses: fully opening https://* is a necessary condition for an outbound client, while arbitrary remote http://* plaintext traffic is not allowed.

Environment Variables (env) and Child Processes (process)

  • env allowlist: HOME, TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR, HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY, plus the lowercase forms http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy, and the wildcard SA_*. Proxy and certificate-path variables appear in pairs, covering both case conventions.
  • process: the current sap.json no longer declares a process section — the old documentation's “spawning child processes is completely forbidden” wording is outdated. Since 2026-09 the plugin uses a curl child process for proxy + TLS (see “Transport Layer” below); this is currently the most stable path.

Transport Layer: The curl Child Process Takes Priority

After the 2026-09 rewrite, HTTPS requests go through the system curl child process by default (curlHttpPost), with curl handling proxy authentication, TLS, and chunked encoding — this is the most stable combination in measurement (the earlier native Zig TLS path was unstable in proxy scenarios). The hand-assembled HTTP/1.0 implementation is kept as a fallback. The request body is relayed through the temporary file /tmp/curl_body_tmp.json and deleted after use.

Retry Mechanism

httpRequestExec uniformly wraps retries: both the first request and follow-up requests after tool calls go through the same entry point.

ItemRule
Retry conditionsHTTP 429, 5xx, transient network errors; other 4xx are not retried
CountAt most 5 retries (6 attempts in total)
BackoffExponential backoff of 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 seconds
Retry-AfterWhen the response header is present, take “the larger of the backoff and Retry-After”, capped at 5 minutes

Native SSE: sa_http_client_sse_turn

A high-level native API that completes a whole turn of “SSE POST + incremental event parsing + live stdout output + tool-call accumulation” in one call (line 68 of sa_http_client.sai):

@extern sa_http_client_sse_turn(&url: ptr, url_len: u64, &body: ptr, body_len: u64,
    &key: ptr, key_len: u64, api_mode: u64,
    &out_text: ptr, &out_text_len: ptr, &out_calls: ptr, &out_calls_len: ptr) -> u32
  • api_mode: 0 = Responses API, 1 = Chat Completions;
  • Supports both the Responses API (output_text.delta, function_call argument fragments, completed) and Chat (content delta, tool_calls routed by index);
  • Multiple tool calls: fragments are routed by call_id (Responses) or index (Chat), supporting parallel / out-of-order delivery;
  • SSE specification details: CRLF separators, multi-line data: joined with \n, and [DONE] termination;
  • Return value: 0 = text complete, 1 = tool calls present, 2 = error;
  • Retries apply only to the initial POST (rules as above); there are no retries once the stream has started — a mid-stream failure returns an error directly.

Companion release function: sa_http_client_sse_turn_free(ptr, len). The main consumer is scodex-mini: A Minimal Codex Written in SLA (the Responses / Chat dual mode with stream:true).

Request Lifecycle and Handle Conventions

Both ABIs follow the same ownership pipeline:

  1. Construct the client: sa_http_client_new (or _new_v2) produces an opaque ptr handle. A non-zero use_tls enables TLS; v2 can additionally take a CA bundle path.
  2. Construct the request: req_new (or req_new_v2 / req_new_joined) binds the method and URL; then req_add_header* and req_set_body* append headers and body. The method is represented by a u8 discriminant: GET=1, POST=2, PUT=3, DELETE=4 (see the HttpMethod enum in src/http_saasm_api.zig and docs/http_client_v2_abi.md).
  3. Send: synchronously via req_send (blocking until the response is ready); asynchronously via req_send_async to get an operation handle, then async_poll / async_take_response. The asynchronous implementation clones and holds the request data, so the caller may release its own request handle right after issuing the async send.
  4. Read the response: resp_status reads the status code; the response body has two paths — the one-shot resp_body_slice / resp_body_ptr + resp_body_len (small responses), or resp_body_reader + resp_read_chunk (large responses / streaming chunks).
  5. Release: explicitly call the ..._free family in reverse order of creation. Pointers to the response body and headers are held by the response and become invalid immediately when the response is released; the reader is released separately by body_reader_free.
WarningThe return values of v1 functions follow the host descriptor's AbiStatus caliber (src/plugin_api.zig): ok=0, unknown_command=1, failed=2, etc. Null pointer arguments, invalid methods, and the like all return failed(2). The seven v2 status codes are unrelated to this; they are a separate set of values — do not mix the judgment logic.

The v1 Function Surface (Contract Excerpted Verbatim)

Source: sa_http_client.sai. The current v1 block has 22 externs in total; the four-plugin joint evaluation document (2026-06-15) recorded 18 at the time, after which 4 legacy WebSocket exports were added (see the next section).

Client and Request Construction

SignatureSemantics
sa_http_client_new(use_tls: u8, &out_client: ptr) -> u32Creates a client; a non-zero use_tls enables TLS. One switch toggles TLS, avoiding two client sets
sa_http_client_req_new(client: ptr, method: u8, &url: ptr, url_len: u64, &out_req: ptr) -> u32Creates a request from a complete URL; the URL is copied into the request handle
sa_http_client_req_new_joined(client: ptr, method: u8, &target: ptr, target_len: u64, &path: ptr, path_len: u64, preserve_base_path: u8, &out_req: ptr) -> u32Joins an “upstream origin + request path” into the final URL. With preserve_base_path=0 it is directly origin + path (adding a / if the path does not start with one); with a non-zero value it preserves the target's own base path, and when the base ends with /v1 and the relative path starts with v1/ it removes the duplicated segment. Typically used for OpenAI-compatible gateway forwarding
sa_http_client_req_add_header(req: ptr, &key: ptr, key_len: u64, &val: ptr, val_len: u64) -> u32Appends a request header (key and value are both copied)
sa_http_client_req_add_openai_auth(req: ptr, &key: ptr, key_len: u64) -> u32Writes two authentication headers at once: authorization: Bearer <key> and x-api-key: <key>; an empty key is a side-effect-free no-op returning ok
sa_http_client_req_set_body(req: ptr, &body: ptr, body_len: u64) -> u32Sets the request body (copied)

Sending and Asynchrony

SignatureSemantics
sa_http_client_req_send(req: ptr, &out_resp: ptr) -> u32Synchronous send, blocking until a response handle is obtained
sa_http_client_req_send_async(req: ptr, &out_op: ptr) -> u32Asynchronous send, returning an operation handle; the operation clones the request internally, so the caller may then req_free
sa_http_client_async_poll(op: ptr, &out_ready: ptr) -> u32Non-blocking poll: out_ready of 1 means a terminal state (including failure), 0 means not ready; the function itself returns ok
sa_http_client_async_take_response(op: ptr, &out_resp: ptr) -> u32Takes the response; it can be taken only once — not ready or already taken returns failed
sa_http_client_async_free(op: ptr) -> u32Releases the asynchronous operation and its cloned data

Response Reading

SignatureSemantics
sa_http_client_resp_status(resp: ptr) -> u16The HTTP status code; returns 0 when resp is null
sa_http_client_resp_get_header(resp: ptr, &key: ptr, key_len: u64, &out_val: ptr, &out_len: ptr) -> u32Looks up a response header by name (case-insensitive), returning a borrowed value pointer and length
sa_http_client_resp_body_slice(resp: ptr, &out_body: ptr, &out_len: ptr) -> u32Borrows the whole response-body slice
sa_http_client_resp_body_ptr(resp: ptr) -> ptrTakes the response-body pointer directly
sa_http_client_resp_body_len(resp: ptr) -> u64Takes the response-body length directly
sa_http_client_resp_body_reader(resp: ptr, &out_reader: ptr) -> u32Obtains a streaming reader (large responses / chunked / SSE)
sa_http_client_resp_read_chunk(reader: ptr, &buf: ptr, cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> u32Reads one chunk into the caller's buffer; the actual length is written to out_len

Release

SignatureSemantics
sa_http_client_resp_free(resp: ptr) -> u32Releases the response; body/header pointers are invalid afterwards
sa_http_client_body_reader_free(reader: ptr) -> u32Releases the streaming reader
sa_http_client_req_free(req: ptr) -> u32Releases the request
sa_http_client_free(client: ptr) -> u32Releases the client

Legacy Blocking WebSocket Exports (4)

The Compatibility section of the README explains: these four symbols already existed and were referenced by native code, and are now declared into the .sa contract so the symbols are visible; the semantics remain blocking, and new code should use v2 instead.

SignatureSemantics
sa_http_client_websocket_connect(client: ptr, &url: ptr, url_len: u64, &out_ws: ptr) -> u32Establishes a WebSocket connection (blocking)
sa_http_websocket_read(ws: ptr, max_len: u64, &out_opcode: ptr, &out_ptr: ptr, &out_len: ptr) -> u32Reads one frame (blocking)
sa_http_websocket_write(ws: ptr, opcode: u8, &data: ptr, data_len: u64) -> u32Writes one frame (blocking)
sa_http_websocket_free(ws: ptr) -> u32Closes and releases

CLI Subcommands

The plugin also exposes host commands (the usage strings are taken verbatim from the error hints in src/plugin.zig):

usage: sa http-client get    [--ca-bundle <path>] [--header name:value] <url>
usage: sa http-client post   [--ca-bundle <path>] [--header name:value] <url> <body>
usage: sa http-client stream [--ca-bundle <path>] [--header name:value] <url> [body]
  • On success, get first prints status: <code> and then outputs the response body (the response buffer cap is max_append_size = 2 MiB).
  • post treats the first non-option argument as the URL and the second as the body, and forwards each --header.
  • stream incrementally forwards the response body in 1024-byte chunks (chunked/SSE without buffering to disk); given a body, it automatically uses POST.
  • --ca-bundle loads a custom CA certificate (made absolute, then injected into the trust chain, with system certificate rescanning disabled).
  • CLI errors uniformly carry the prefix error[SA-HTTP-CLIENT-CLI]: plus a help: line, and the process exit code is 1.

The v2 Surface: The Seven Status Codes Explained One by One

Every v2 operation returns one of the following stable status codes (confirmed by both the README and docs/http_client_v2_abi.md; the tests in tests/plugin_test.zig assert each value):

ValueNameMeaning and trigger scenarios
0okThe operation completed. For a write operation it means out_written equals the payload length
1would_blockA zero-timeout poll or a non-blocking operation is not ready. For example, when websocket_poll_v2(..., timeout_ms=0) has none of the events of interest
2closedThe peer closed, cancellation completed, or the transport is no longer usable. A legitimate peer close frame appears as closed on the read interface; poll/take on a cancelled asynchronous operation also returns it
3timeoutA positive deadline expired. When the request-level deadline (req_set_timeout_v2) expires, req_send_v2 returns this value and produces no response
4too_largeA configured body/message limit was exceeded. The response body exceeds req_set_max_response_bytes_v2, or a WebSocket frame exceeds the limit (an over-limit frame is rejected before allocation)
5invalidAn argument, URI, request header, handshake, or WebSocket frame is invalid. For example, a method discriminant outside 1..4, setting a limit to 0, or an unparseable URI
6io_errorA transport or allocator failure, with no more specific status code available

The WebSocket polling interest bits and event bits share one set of values: readable=1, writable=2, closed=4. Output slots are zeroed before any validation or I/O, so stale values are never read.

v2 Request Increments

Signature (excerpted from the .sa contract)Semantics
sa_http_client_new_v2(use_tls: u8, &ca_bundle_path: ptr, ca_bundle_path_len: u64, &out_client: ptr) -> u32A CA bundle path (nullable) can be specified when creating the client
sa_http_client_req_new_v2(client: ptr, method: u8, &url: ptr, url_len: u64, &out_req: ptr) -> u32Validated request construction (the method discriminant follows v1)
sa_http_client_req_add_header_v2(...) / sa_http_client_req_set_body_v2(...)Validated header and body writes
sa_http_client_req_set_timeout_v2(req: ptr, timeout_ms: u32) -> u32Sets the deadline for the whole request (milliseconds); 0 disables it. Once transport establishment completes, the deadline observably takes effect
sa_http_client_req_set_max_response_bytes_v2(req: ptr, max_bytes: u64) -> u32A caller-defined response-body limit; must be non-zero, default 16 MiB
sa_http_client_req_send_v2(req: ptr, &out_resp: ptr) -> u32Synchronous send; a 302 is handed directly to the caller, not followed hiddenly
sa_http_client_req_send_async_v2 / sa_http_client_async_poll_v2(op, timeout_ms, &ready) / sa_http_client_async_take_response_v2 / sa_http_client_async_cancel_v2(op) / sa_http_client_async_free_v2Conditional asynchronous polling (with timeout), cancellation, and response handover. poll returns ready=1 for every terminal state (timeout, cancellation=closed, over-limit, I/O failure); the response can be taken only once
NoteCancellation is implemented by shutting down the published socket to wake blocked send/read calls. Zig 0.17.0 does not expose the socket before DNS resolution, TCP connect, and TLS initialization complete, so those three stages cannot be hard-interrupted by this ABI — cancellation is observed immediately after them, and async_free_v2 may wait for the operating system to finish connect teardown. Not following redirects also keeps cancellation always bound to a single file descriptor.

v2 WebSocket Increments

SignatureSemantics
sa_http_client_websocket_connect_v2(client, &url, url_len, timeout_ms, &ws)ws:// uses TCP, wss:// uses TLS
sa_http_client_websocket_connect_unix_v2(client, &socket_path, socket_path_len, &url, url_len, timeout_ms, &ws)A Unix-domain socket as the physical transport, plus a logical URL providing Host, path, and query semantics; Unix mode rejects wss://
sa_http_client_req_websocket_connect_v2(req, timeout_ms, &ws) / ..._unix_v2Reuses the custom headers in the request handle for the handshake (TCP/TLS or Unix transport)
sa_http_websocket_poll_v2(ws, interests, timeout_ms, &events)Polls by interest bits; not ready with timeout_ms=0 returns would_block, a positive timeout expiring returns timeout
sa_http_websocket_read_v2(ws, max_len, &opcode, &ptr, &len)Non-blocking after poll. Text opcode=1, binary opcode=2; reassembles continuation frames, answers ping/pong internally, validates close; an invalid or over-limit frame closes the transport to avoid stream misalignment. The returned message pointer is borrowed from the ws handle and stays valid until the next successful read or free_v2; the caller must not free it
sa_http_websocket_write_v2(ws, opcode, &data, data_len, &written)Writes one complete, masked client message; on ok, written == payload length, and 0 for other statuses. Text must be UTF-8; ping/pong payloads ≤125 bytes; all messages ≤16 MiB
sa_http_websocket_close_v2(ws, code: u16, &reason, reason_len)Accepts a legitimate RFC 6455 close code and a UTF-8 reason of ≤123 bytes
sa_http_websocket_free_v2(ws)Closes the transport and returns the retained client reference

The 16 MiB message limit comes from max_v2_message_bytes. TLS mode retains the original connection object, its TLS state, and the bytes buffered after upgrade, and never copies a raw TLS file descriptor.

v2 Ownership Rules

  • A v2 request retains its client until the request is released; an async operation retains the cloned request and the client until the async operation is released; a WebSocket retains the client and the connection until the ws is released.
  • Therefore the owner may call sa_http_client_free immediately after creating these handles, and the handles remain valid.
  • Response body/header pointers are owned by the response and become invalid when the response is released.
  • Running a concurrent free on the same handle concurrently with other calls is illegal; WebSocket poll/read/write/close are serialized internally.

v1 → v2 Migration Comparison

Needv1 approachv2 approach
Judging the resultAbiStatus (0=ok / 2=failed), with limited informationSeven stable status codes, distinguishing timeout, over-limit, cancellation, and peer close
TimeoutNo timeout API at all (listed as a gap by the evaluation document)req_set_timeout_v2 request-level deadline; poll with a millisecond timeout
Response-body limitNonereq_set_max_response_bytes_v2 (default 16 MiB, must be non-zero)
CancellationNoneasync_cancel_v2, waking blocked I/O by shutting down the socket
RedirectsUnderlying-layer behaviorA 302 is handed to the caller as-is, not followed hiddenly
WebSocket4 legacy blocking exportsThree transports (TCP/TLS/Unix) + polling event bits + frame reassembly + masking + protocol close
Handle lifetimeYou must keep the client alive yourselfrequest/async/ws each retain a client reference, so the owner may free the client early

Out-of-Scope Items (Explicitly Declared Not Done in the Documentation)

WarningThe product target is Linux x86_64. The following items are explicitly placed outside the base scope by the README and the v2 ABI document: HTTP/2, HTTP/3, strict non-blocking TLS record recovery (a partially timed-out TLS record makes the connection unusable and it is closed rather than replayed), and interruptible DNS. Note that “automatic retry” was moved out of the out-of-scope list in 2026-09: httpRequestExec now retries 429/5xx/transient network errors up to 5 times (see “Retry Mechanism” above). v2 still does not follow redirects automatically; the legacy blocking WebSocket is kept for compatibility only (the new WebSocket client capability is in sa_std/ws_client.sai). The evaluation document also notes the lack of an mTLS client-certificate API (suggested shape client_set_cert) — the current contract indeed has none.
The caliber must likewise be distinguished: on the SCI side, docs/http_client_plugin.md labels “zero-copy cooperation with sa_net_uring” as a target direction, and describes "grants": ["net_tx:..."] and certificate pinning as target designs of the host permission layer; its example signatures (such as a req_send with a body parameter, returning -> i32!) also differ from the real contract. The actual permission model is the sap.json net/env/certificate-directory allowlist in the earlier part of this page, not grants/pinning fields.

End-to-End Examples (Real Code)

Complete SA Source-Level Flow: Construct → Send → Read Body → Release

Source: D:/projects/sla/sci/demos/rosetta/301_http_client_saasm/main.sa (sending a POST to a local loopback address and validating the response). The backbone is excerpted below, with signatures and call order preserved as in the original:

@extern sa_http_client_new(use_tls: u8, &out_client: ptr) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_req_new(client: ptr, method: u8, &url: ptr, url_len: u64, &out_req: ptr) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_req_add_header(req: ptr, &key: ptr, key_len: u64, &val: ptr, val_len: u64) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_req_set_body(req: ptr, &body: ptr, body_len: u64) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_req_send(req: ptr, &out_resp: ptr) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_resp_status(resp: ptr) -> u16
@extern sa_http_client_resp_body_reader(resp: ptr, &out_reader: ptr) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_resp_read_chunk(reader: ptr, &buf: ptr, cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> u32
; ... 以及四个 ^xxx 形式的释放导出

@const URL  = utf8:"http://127.0.0.1:18090/echo"
@const KEY  = utf8:"content-type"
@const VAL  = utf8:"text/plain"
@const BODY = utf8:"hello from saasm"

@main() -> i32!:
L_ENTRY:
    client_slot = stack_alloc 8
    req_slot    = stack_alloc 8
    resp_slot   = stack_alloc 8
    reader_slot = stack_alloc 8
    buf         = stack_alloc 64        ; #def Buf_SIZE = 64

    client_status = call @sa_http_client_new(0, &client_slot)
    !client_status                       ; 显式释放该临时值（所有权语句）
    client = load client_slot+0 as ptr

    req_status = call @sa_http_client_req_new(client, 2, &URL, 27, &req_slot)
    !req_status                         ; 方法 2 = POST，27 = URL 字节数
    req = load req_slot+0 as ptr

    hdr_status  = call @sa_http_client_req_add_header(req, &KEY, 12, &VAL, 10)
    body_status = call @sa_http_client_req_set_body(req, &BODY, 16)
    send_status = call @sa_http_client_req_send(req, &resp_slot)

    resp   = load resp_slot+0 as ptr
    status = call @sa_http_client_resp_status(resp)      ; 期望 200
    reader_status = call @sa_http_client_resp_body_reader(resp, &reader_slot)
    reader = load reader_slot+0 as ptr
    read_status = call @sa_http_client_resp_read_chunk(reader, &buf, 64, &read_len_slot)

    call @sa_http_client_body_reader_free(^reader)
    call @sa_http_client_resp_free(^resp)
    call @sa_http_client_req_free(^req)
    call @sa_http_client_free(^client)

The ^resp / ^req / ^client parameter forms in the same demo show SA's “release means null out” ownership markers at the SA layer. For typesetting, the excerpt inlines constants such as the original's #def URL_LEN = 27 as literal numbers and omits some status-slot declarations; the verbatim compilable version is the source file above; statements of the form !client_status are SA's ownership release form: per sci/docs/tutorial/beginner_guide.md, “! explicitly releases an owned resource or ends a borrow”, the compiler does not insert drops automatically, and every live register must be !-ed one by one before returning (llm_cheat_sheet.md lists omitting it as a MemoryLeak trap).

Minimal VM FFI Verification

Source: D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_vm/tests/http_client_test.sa — the dynamic VM calling the plugin through FFI in a minimal closed loop (create, then release immediately):

@extern sa_http_client_new(use_tls: u32, &out_client: ptr) -> u32
@extern sa_http_client_free(client: ptr) -> u32

@main() -> i32:
L_ENTRY:
    client_slot = stack_alloc 8
    status = call @sa_http_client_new(0, &client_slot)
    ok = eq status, 0
    br ok -> L_FREE, L_ERR

Note: here use_tls is written as u32, which disagrees with the u8 in the .sa contract; that is this test's own widening form — sa_http_client.sai is authoritative.

CLI Session Example (from Assertions in tests/plugin_test.zig)

# 回环 GET：stdout 为 "status: 200\nhello from loopback\n"
sa http-client get http://127.0.0.1:<port>/hello

# POST 转发自定义头与 body
sa http-client post --header content-type: text/plain http://127.0.0.1:<port>/submit "payload body"

# chunked SSE 增量转发，stdout 逐块得到 "data: first\n\ndata: second\n\n"
sa http-client stream http://127.0.0.1:<port>/events

# 自签名 HTTPS + 自定义 CA bundle（测试里用 openssl s_server 起本地 TLS 服务）
sa http-client get --ca-bundle server.crt https://localhost:18443/

In the repository, these command lines are invoked as argv arrays through runHttpClientCommand (D:/projects/sla/sa_plugin_http_client/tests/plugin_test.zig); the diagnostic output when the URL is missing is error[SA-HTTP-CLIENT-CLI]: missing required HTTP client URL plus a usage line.

The v2 Asynchronous and Cancellation Call Shape

The repository has no SA source-level example for v2 (examples/get.sa is a deliberately empty placeholder file, only hinting to use sa http-client get https://example.com via the CLI). The call form based on the contract signatures is as follows (pseudocode, showing order only):

c   = sa_http_client_new_v2(0, null, 0)                 ; 或传 CA bundle 路径
req = sa_http_client_req_new_v2(c, 1, url)
sa_http_client_req_set_timeout_v2(req, 20)              ; 20ms 截止时间
sa_http_client_req_set_max_response_bytes_v2(req, 65536)
op  = sa_http_client_req_send_async_v2(req)
sa_http_client_req_free(req)                            ; op 已克隆请求
sa_http_client_free(c)                                  ; op 同时保留 client 引用
loop: st = sa_http_client_async_poll_v2(op, 100, &ready); until ready == 1
st  = sa_http_client_async_take_response_v2(op, &resp)  ; closed 表示已被取消
sa_http_client_async_free_v2(op)

The v2 behavioral details (a deadline expiring returns timeout, over-limit returns too_large, cancelling twice is idempotent, poll returns closed and take returns a null handle, etc.) are all backed by Zig tests, whose source is likewise tests/plugin_test.zig.
